name: SciQ
description: A dataset of 13,679 multiple choice science exam questions crowdsourced using a novel method that leverages a large corpus of domain-specific text and existing questions to aid question generation. The dataset includes questions with associated passages, correct answers, and distractor options.

creator.name: Johannes Welbl, Nelson F. Liu, Matt Gardner
creator.affiliation: University College London, University of Washington, Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence

citeAs: Welbl, J., Liu, N. F., & Gardner, M. (2017). Crowdsourcing Multiple Choice Science Questions. arXiv:1707.06209v1 [cs.HC]
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected through a two-step crowdsourcing process on Amazon Mechanical Turk. First, crowd workers were shown three filtered textbook paragraphs and asked to select one and formulate a question about it. Second, another worker validated the question-answer pair and generated three distractors, aided by model-generated suggestions. Workers were required to have Master's status on AMT.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data source consisted of 28 science study textbooks from various online learning resources including CK-12 and OpenStax, covering biology, chemistry, earth science and physics, spanning elementary level to college introductory material. The books were shared under Creative Commons License.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A rule-based document filter was applied to individual paragraphs from the base corpus. The filter classified sentences and accepted paragraphs if a minimum number of sentences passed. Filter rules included lexical, grammatical, pragmatical and complexity-based criteria, such as filtering out questions, exclamations, sentences without verb phrases, those with modal verbs, imperative phrases, demonstrative pronouns, personal pronouns other than third-person, sentences with less than 6 or more than 18 tokens, and various other criteria to identify simple declarative statements.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The annotation process involved two crowdsourcing tasks: (1) Question formulation task where workers were shown three filtered textbook paragraphs, selected one, and formulated a question with an answer (6-30 words for question, up to 3 words for answer). (2) Distractor selection task where workers validated the question-answer pair and either selected up to two from six model-suggested distractors or wrote their own, with a requirement to write at least one distractor themselves for a total of three distractors. Workers were paid $0.30 per HIT for the first task and $0.20 per HIT for the second task. 92.8% of questions passed quality control.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: In the distractor selection task, crowd workers found the predicted distractors good enough to include approximately half of the time, resulting in 36.1% of the distractors in the final dataset being generated by the model. Acceptance rates were higher for short answers and almost none were accepted for very long answers.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each question has one correct answer and three distractors (incorrect answer options), for a total of four answer options per question.
rai:annotatorDemographics: 175 workers participated in the crowdsourcing project. Workers were required to have Amazon Mechanical Turk Master's status.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: A distractor ranking model was used to suggest answer distractors. The model used a random forest classifier trained on 3,705 science exam questions (4th and 8th grade) with features including GloVe embeddings, POS-tag consistency, string edit distance, WordNet-based hypernymy indicators, and knowledge-base links from OpenIE triples extracted from Simple Wikipedia. The model achieved 99.4% training and 94.2% validation accuracy.
rai:dataLimitations: A small percentage of passages were obtained from unreleasable texts, so the direct answer version of SciQ is slightly smaller (10,481 questions in train, 887 in dev, 884 in test) compared to the multiple choice version (11,679 in train, 1,000 in dev, 1,000 in test). Neural models did not outperform simple information retrieval baselines on the multiple choice version, suggesting the dataset is useful for studying reading comprehension models in medium-data settings.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset has two versions: (1) Multiple choice version where systems must select the correct answer from four options using background knowledge, without the passage. (2) Direct answer version where systems are given the passage and question and must predict the span within the passage that answers the question. The dataset can be used for training models on science exam QA tasks. When used as additional training data with existing questions, accuracy improvements were observed on real 4th and 8th grade science exams (improvements of 4.3-7.8% for 4th grade and 1.8-3.3% for 8th grade).
